documents.html:
Document control

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
SOP reference SOP-03 – Personal Protective Equipment
Linked SSOW SSOW-03 – Personal Protective Equipment
Version 1.0
Prepared by James Pickard (Managing Director)
Approved by Mathew Pickard (Director)
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner if SSOW-03 changes, after an accident or near miss, or when the equipment or task changes

1. Purpose

This SOP sets out the standard method for issuing, checking, wearing, looking after and replacing personal protective equipment (PPE) at Pickard Event Services, including overhead work zones, so that it is done the same way every time. The hazards, risk ratings, PPE matrix and PPE specification are in SSOW-03 – Personal Protective Equipment, which must be read with this SOP. PPE is the last line of defence, used alongside other controls, not instead of them.

2. Scope

This SOP applies whenever anyone enters a work area at Unit 1, Brickyard Road or at a client event site. Hi-vis and safety footwear are worn at all times in the warehouse, yard and on build and break; gloves, respirators and eye protection are worn for the tasks listed in the SSOW-03 matrix; and hard hats are worn whenever overhead work is in progress.

Applies to:

  • Employees, agency or casual crew, subcontractors and visitors entering work areas.
  • Unit 1, Brickyard Road: warehouse, mezzanine, loading area and yard.
  • Client event sites: venues, exhibition halls and outdoor sites, during build and break.
  • All PPE listed in section 6, from issue and training through to replacement and stock checks.

Does not cover:

  • The office, where there is no warehouse access and no PPE is required.
  • The method for working at height itself; see H5 – Working at Height.
  • Choosing PPE for a specific chemical product; follow the product COSHH sheet and safety data sheet under H21 – COSHH.
  • Forklift loading and unloading; see SOP-01 and SSOW-01 (the PPE in this SOP still applies).

3. Responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Approves SSOW-03 and this SOP; provides suitable PPE free of charge; makes sure enough stock is held
Warehouse Manager Issues PPE and keeps the PPE issue record; arranges face-fit testing; checks PPE is worn; replaces damaged PPE; checks stock monthly; stops work where PPE is missing
Crew chief / supervisor on site Briefs PPE requirements at the start of each shift or event; sets up, signs and removes overhead work zones; checks PPE before work starts and during the shift
All staff and crew Wear the PPE required; check it before use; look after it; report loss, damage or a poor fit straight away; do not alter PPE
Visitors and contractors Wear the PPE given to them before entering work areas, and follow instructions

4. Definitions

Term Meaning
PPE Personal protective equipment: hi-vis, safety footwear, gloves, respirators, hard hats and eye protection
RPE Respiratory protective equipment: disposable FFP3 respirators and reusable half-mask respirators
Face-fit test A test by a competent fit tester that a tight-fitting respirator seals on the wearer’s face, for a specific make and model
Fit check The wearer’s own check each time a respirator is put on: cover it and breathe in and out to check for leaks
Overhead work zone A coned, barriered or taped area below and around overhead work, signed “Overhead work in progress – hard hats must be worn”
PPE matrix The SSOW-03 table showing which PPE each area or task needs
COSHH sheet The product sheet stating the gloves, eye protection and RPE needed
Bump cap A cap that protects against knocks on fixed objects only; not a substitute for a hard hat under overhead work

5. Competence and authorisation

  • Only people who have received PPE training on induction may work in the warehouse, yard or on event sites.
  • Only people who have passed a face-fit test for the specific make and model of tight-fitting respirator (FFP3 or half-mask) may use that respirator.
  • Face-fit tests are carried out by a competent fit tester and repeated when the model changes, when the wearer’s face shape changes (weight, dental work), or at least every 2 years.
  • Respirator wearers must be clean-shaven where the mask seals. Anyone who cannot be is given a powered or loose-fitting hood respirator instead.
  • Only the crew chief or supervisor sets up and removes overhead work zones.
  • Visitors and contractors may enter work areas only once they are wearing the PPE given to them.
  • Everyone signs the staff acknowledgement record for this SOP and the briefing record for SSOW-03.

6. Equipment, PPE and materials

Item Requirement
Hi-vis vest or jacket EN ISO 20471; Class 2 vest minimum; Class 3 jacket for yards and outdoor sites in poor light
Safety footwear EN ISO 20345; S3 (or S1P minimum indoors)
Handling and cut-resistant gloves EN 388; cut level C or above for aluminium profile and sharp edges
Chemical-resistant gloves EN ISO 374-1; nitrile, as stated on the SDS and COSHH sheet
Respirators FFP3 disposable (EN 149) or half-mask with A2P3 filters where the COSHH sheet says; face-fit tested
Hard hat EN 397; chin strap for work at height or in MEWPs; within expiry date
Bump cap EN 812; low-headroom work only, never under overhead work
Eye protection EN 166; glasses, goggles for chemical splash, face shield for battery work
Overhead work zone kit Cones, barriers or tape, and overhead work signs
Paperwork PPE issue record, COSHH sheets and safety data sheets, face-fit test certificates

Full specifications and “replace when” conditions are in the SSOW-03 PPE specification table.

7. Procedure

Follow these steps in order, using the PPE matrix in SSOW-03 to decide what is needed for each area and task. Where a venue or principal contractor has its own rules, follow whichever is stricter.

7.1 Issue and training

  1. Issue core PPE on day one. Issue every new employee and casual crew member, free of charge and in the right size, a hi-vis vest, safety footwear, general handling gloves and cut-resistant gloves.
  2. Issue task PPE. Issue hard hats, chemical gloves, eye protection and respirators to those whose tasks need them, or hold them as pool stock for event sites.
  3. Record each issue. Enter the date, name, item and size on the PPE issue record and have the person receiving it sign it.
  4. Train on induction. Give PPE training covering the PPE matrix, how to check, fit, clean and store PPE, its limits, and how to report defects.
  5. Face-fit test respirator wearers. Arrange a face-fit test by a competent fit tester for each person who needs a tight-fitting respirator, for that make and model, and record the result and model on the PPE issue record.
  6. Deal with fit problems. Where PPE is uncomfortable or ill-fitting, provide an alternative, for example different glove sizes, wide-fit safety footwear, or female-fit hi-vis and hard hats.

Hold point: Do not use a tight-fitting respirator until you have passed a face-fit test for that make and model and are clean-shaven where the mask seals.

7.2 Before starting work

  1. Brief the PPE for the job. At the start of each shift or event, the crew chief or supervisor briefs the PPE needed, including any venue or principal contractor rules.
  2. Check your hi-vis. It must be clean, bright, with reflective tape intact, and fastened.
  3. Check your footwear. Toe caps must not be exposed or dented, soles must be intact with grip, and laces done up.
  4. Check your gloves. They must be the right type for the task (general, cut-resistant or chemical) with no holes or tears.
  5. Check your respirator. It must be the correct type and filter, with straps and valve intact and in date. Do a fit check every time you put it on.
  6. Check your hard hat. The shell must not be cracked, the harness adjusted to fit, within its expiry date, and the chin strap fitted when working at height.
  7. Swap defective PPE. Do not use defective PPE. Swap it from stock straight away and hand the damaged item to the Warehouse Manager.
  8. Check others before work starts. The crew chief or supervisor checks that everyone is wearing the required PPE before the task begins.

Hold point: No PPE, no work. Anyone without the required PPE does not start the task until it is provided.

7.3 Overhead work: hard hat zones

  1. Set up the zone first. Before overhead work starts (mobile towers, MEWPs, truss or rigging, ladders above head height, mezzanine loading, high racking), the crew chief sets up an overhead work zone below and around the work with cones, barriers or tape.
  2. Sign the zone. Display the sign “Overhead work in progress – hard hats must be worn”.
  3. Size the zone. Extend the zone at least 2 m beyond the edge of the work platform, and further for high work or outdoors in wind, so it catches anything that could fall or bounce.
  4. Hard hats on for everyone in the zone. Everyone inside the zone wears a hard hat, including people passing through, the MEWP ground person and anyone steadying a ladder. People on the platform fasten their chin straps.
  5. Keep people out. Keep people out of the zone wherever possible. Nobody stands directly below a person working at height or a suspended load.
  6. Control falling objects. Tether tools and lift materials in bags or by line; never throw them (see H5).
  7. Follow venue rules. At event sites, follow the venue’s hard hat rules, which may require hard hats throughout the hall during build and break.
  8. Remove the zone when finished. When overhead work finishes, the crew chief removes the zone and signage. Hard hats are then no longer mandatory unless another overhead zone or venue rule applies.

Hold point: No overhead work starts until the zone is set up and signed and everyone inside it is wearing a hard hat.

7.4 During work

  1. Wear PPE properly for the whole task. Keep hi-vis fastened and not covered by other clothing. Keep your respirator on while dust or vapour is present; removing it even briefly removes the protection.
  2. Replace damaged PPE. If PPE is damaged during work, stop, move to a safe area and replace it before carrying on.
  3. Supervise PPE use. Supervisors check PPE use during the shift and correct anyone not wearing it.

Hold point: If anyone is seen without the required PPE, stop the task until they have moved to a safe area and put it on.

7.5 After use: cleaning, storage and replacement

  1. Clean reusable PPE. Clean reusable PPE after use as the manufacturer advises.
  2. Store it correctly. Store PPE dry, clean and out of direct sunlight. Keep respirators in a sealed bag or box away from contaminants. Do not leave hard hats in vehicles in sunlight or near solvents.
  3. Dispose of single-use items. Throw away FFP3 masks and disposable gloves after the shift or when contaminated. Put contaminated chemical gloves in the waste bin stated on the COSHH sheet.
  4. Replace worn PPE. Replace PPE when it meets the “replace when” conditions in the SSOW-03 specification table, or at the manufacturer’s expiry date. Replacement is free of charge.
  5. Check stock monthly. The Warehouse Manager checks PPE stock monthly, including sizes, filters and hard hat expiry dates, and re-orders before stocks run low.

8. Completion checks

Check Standard
PPE worn Everyone in the work area wore the PPE in the matrix for the whole task
Overhead work zones Removed with their signs once overhead work finished
Reusable PPE Cleaned and stored dry, clean and out of direct sunlight
Respirators Stored in a sealed bag or box away from contaminants
Disposable PPE Thrown away after the shift; contaminated chemical gloves in the correct bin
Defective PPE Handed to the Warehouse Manager; replacement issued
Records PPE issued during the job entered on the PPE issue record and signed

9. If something goes wrong

Situation Action
Person seen without required PPE Stop the task; the person moves to a safe area and puts on the PPE before restarting
PPE lost, damaged or out of stock Do not start or continue the task until PPE is provided; report to the Warehouse Manager
PPE damaged during work Stop, move to a safe area and replace it from stock
PPE causes discomfort, skin reaction, poor fit, or affects vision or hearing Move to safety before removing it; report it; an alternative is found
Visitor or contractor refuses PPE Do not allow them into the work area
Repeated failure to wear PPE Recorded and dealt with by the Warehouse Manager or Managing Director under the company disciplinary procedure
Hard hat takes a significant impact Take it out of use and replace it

See SSOW-03 – Personal Protective Equipment for the full non-compliance arrangements and the duties of the company and staff under the PPE at Work Regulations.

10. Records

Record Completed by Kept by
PPE issue record (date, name, item and size, face-fit test result and model, signature) Warehouse Manager and person receiving PPE Warehouse Manager
Face-fit test certificates Competent fit tester Warehouse Manager
Induction checklist (including PPE training) Warehouse Manager Warehouse Manager
Record of repeated failure to wear PPE Warehouse Manager or Managing Director Warehouse Manager or Managing Director
SSOW-03 staff and crew briefing record All staff and crew Warehouse Manager
SOP-03 staff acknowledgement record All staff and crew Warehouse Manager

documents.html:
Document details

This safe system of work sets out how everyone works safely day to day in the warehouse at Unit 1, Brickyard Road. It covers the general rules for the whole warehouse and points to the specific SSOWs and risk assessments for higher-risk tasks such as forklift work, work at height, chemicals and lone working.

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
Reference SSOW-04 – Warehouse Operations
Location Unit 1, Brickyard Road: warehouse floor, racking, mezzanine, profile cleaning area, forklift charging point, loading area and yard
Activities Receiving, storing, picking and preparing event equipment; returns from events; checking, cleaning and repairing stock; moving loads by hand, trolley, pallet truck and forklift; housekeeping and waste
Persons at risk Employees, agency or casual crew, visiting drivers, contractors and visitors
Assessor James Pickard
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner after an accident or near miss, a change to the warehouse layout or racking, or new equipment

Key legislation and guidance: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999; Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992; PUWER 1998; LOLER 1998; Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992; Work at Height Regulations 2005; COSHH 2002; Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; HSE HSG76 (Warehousing and storage – a guide to health and safety); HSE HSG136 (Workplace transport safety); SEMA guidance on racking inspection.

Roles and responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Approves this SSOW; provides resources, equipment and training; makes sure inspections are carried out
Warehouse Manager Runs the warehouse day to day; inducts new staff; carries out the daily and weekly checks; keeps records; stops unsafe work
Forklift operators Follow SSOW-01; keep to forklift routes; give way to pedestrians at crossings
All warehouse staff and crew Follow this SSOW; wear PPE (SSOW-03); keep the warehouse tidy; report hazards, damage and near misses
Visitors and contractors Sign in; are escorted; wear the hi-vis and PPE provided; follow instructions

Hazards and risk ratings

Risk = Likelihood (L) × Severity (S), each scored 1–5, as in the H-series risk assessments. Ratings are residual risk, with this SSOW followed. Pedestrian and forklift contact carries the highest residual risk (5, Medium); slips and trips and manual handling are the most frequent sources of minor injury.

Score Likelihood Severity
1 Very unlikely Trivial – no treatment needed
2 Unlikely Minor – first aid only
3 Possible Moderate – medical treatment, up to 7 days off work
4 Likely Major – RIDDOR-reportable or over-7-day injury
5 Almost certain Fatal or permanent disability
Risk score Rating Action required
1–4 Low Maintain current controls; review annually
5–9 Medium Controls adequate but monitor; improve where reasonably practicable
10–16 High Further controls needed before or alongside work; management attention
20–25 Very high Stop work until risk is reduced
Ref Hazard Main controls (section of this SSOW) Residual L × S Rating
WH1 Pedestrian struck by forklift or vehicle Marked walkways, crossing points, hi-vis, SSOW-01 (Stage 1) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
WH2 Slips, trips and falls on the same level Housekeeping, clear aisles, spills cleaned at once (Stage 2) 2 × 2 = 4 Low
WH3 Falling objects from racking or stacks Racking loading rules, inspections, stacking limits (Stage 3) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
WH4 Racking collapse after impact Column guards, damage reporting, SEMA inspection (Stage 3) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
WH5 Falls from the mezzanine or stairs Edge protection, pallet gate, SWL, H5 (Stage 4) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
WH6 Manual handling injuries Handling aids, team lifts, H8 (Stage 5) 2 × 3 = 6 Medium
WH7 Cuts from profile, tools and packaging Gloves, safe knife use, guards (Stages 5 and 7) 2 × 2 = 4 Low
WH8 Chemicals in the profile cleaning area Designated area, COSHH sheets, H21 (Stage 6) 1 × 3 = 3 Low
WH9 Fire from combustible stock, waste or charging Housekeeping, waste removal, charging rules, H19 (Stages 2 and 8) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
WH10 Electrical equipment Pre-use checks, PAT testing (Stage 7) 1 × 4 = 4 Low

Warehouse rules at a glance

These rules are displayed at the warehouse entrance and briefed at induction.

  1. Hi-vis and safety footwear at all times on the warehouse floor, mezzanine, loading area and yard.

  2. Walk in marked walkways. Cross forklift routes only at crossing points, and stop, look and make eye contact with the driver first.

  3. Never walk under a raised load or into a forklift working area.

  4. Keep aisles, walkways, fire exits and fire equipment clear at all times.

  5. Clean up spills straight away, or cone them off and report them.

  6. Heavy items low, light items high. Never climb racking.

  7. Report racking damage straight away – do not use a damaged bay.

  8. Mezzanine pallet gate closed on the operator side whenever the loading point is open.

  9. Use trolleys and pallet trucks – do not carry what you can wheel.

  10. No smoking or vaping in the building.

  11. No forklift work, work at height or heavy lifting alone (SSOW-02).

  12. Report every accident and near miss.

Before work starts

Competence and induction

  • Every new employee, agency or casual worker has a warehouse induction on their first day, before starting work: the rules above, walkways and crossing points, fire exits and assembly point, first aid, welfare facilities, PPE, and how to report hazards. The induction is recorded.

  • Only authorised, certificated operators use the forklift (SSOW-01). Pallet trucks, power tools and the profile cleaning area are used only after instruction.

  • Young workers (under 18) and new starters are supervised and do not use the forklift, work at height or work alone.

Personal protective equipment

Wear PPE as set out in SSOW-03: hi-vis and safety footwear at all times in the warehouse; gloves for handling; chemical gloves and eye protection in the cleaning area; respirators for cutting and sanding; hard hats in overhead work zones.

Opening-up checks (first person in, each day)

The first person in (or the Warehouse Manager) checks and records on the daily warehouse checklist:

  1. Building secure and no signs of break-in, leaks or damage overnight.

  2. Lights working throughout the warehouse, mezzanine and yard.

  3. Fire exits unlocked and clear; fire alarm panel showing no faults; extinguishers in place.

  4. Walkways, aisles and crossing points clear and markings visible.

  5. No spills, loose packaging or trip hazards on the floor.

  6. No obvious racking damage or overloaded bays.

  7. Mezzanine edge protection and pallet gate intact and working.

  8. Forklift pre-use check done by the operator before use (SSOW-01).

  9. First aid kit and eyewash available.

Any defect is reported to the Warehouse Manager. Anything that makes an area unsafe is coned off or tagged out of use until fixed.

Safe system of work – step by step

Stage 1 – Moving around the warehouse: pedestrians and forklifts

  1. Pedestrians use the marked walkways and cross forklift routes only at marked crossing points.

  2. Before crossing, stop, look both ways, and make eye contact with any forklift driver. Wait until the driver has stopped or signalled you on.

  3. Forklift operators travel at walking pace inside the warehouse, sound the horn at blind corners, doorways and the ends of aisles, and give way to pedestrians at crossings.

  4. Nobody enters a forklift working area or exclusion zone, or walks under raised forks or loads.

  5. Do not use mobile phones or wear headphones while walking on forklift routes or operating equipment.

  6. Doors between the warehouse and the office are kept closed; office staff entering the warehouse put on hi-vis and check for forklift movement first.

Stage 2 – Housekeeping

  1. Keep walkways, aisles, crossing points, fire exits, extinguishers, call points, electrical panels and first aid points clear at all times. Nothing is stored in walkways, even temporarily.

  2. Clean as you go: remove packaging, shrink wrap, straps and offcuts to the correct bin as soon as you finish with them.

  3. Clean up spills straight away using the spill kit, or cone them off and report them.

  4. Trailing cables are routed away from walkways or covered with cable protectors.

  5. Returns from events are unloaded to the designated returns area, checked and put away within an agreed time (target: end of the next working day), so the floor does not build up with kit.

  6. Waste is removed to the external skips at least daily. Cardboard and plastic are not allowed to build up inside the building (fire risk, H19).

Stage 3 – Storage and racking

  1. Racking is used only as designed: loads within the safe working load (SWL) shown on the load notice for each bay and beam level. If there is no load notice, the bay is not used until one is fitted.

  2. Pallets are placed squarely on beams with no overhang beyond the manufacturer's limit; damaged pallets are not used.

  3. Heavy items go on lower levels; light items higher. Nothing is stored on top of racking unless designed for it.

  4. Loose items on upper levels are boxed, shrink-wrapped or restrained so they cannot fall.

  5. Long items (aluminium profile, truss, poles) are stored horizontally on cantilever or profile racking, never leaning against walls or racking.

  6. Free-standing stacks of cases or boxes are kept stable and no higher than about 1.8 m (or 3 times the base width, whichever is less) unless designed to stack higher.

  7. Nobody climbs racking. Use the forklift (SSOW-01), or approved steps or a podium for low levels (H5).

  8. Racking damage: any impact, bent upright or beam, missing beam lock or loose floor fixing is reported straight away. The bay is unloaded and taped off until checked. Damage is graded using the SEMA traffic light system: red = unload at once and isolate; amber = unload as soon as possible and repair within 4 weeks; green = monitor.

  9. Racking is visually inspected weekly by the Warehouse Manager and inspected at least annually by a SEMA-approved racking inspector (SARI).

Stage 4 – Mezzanine

  1. The mezzanine SWL (kg/m²) is displayed at the stairs and the loading point, and stored items are kept within it and spread evenly.

  2. Goods are moved to and from the mezzanine by forklift through the pallet safety gate, not carried up or down the stairs.

  3. The pallet gate is always closed on one side: the operator side is closed whenever the loading side is open. The gate is never tied or wedged open.

  4. Nobody leans over the gate or edge protection, or stands below the loading point during loading (exclusion zone marked).

  5. Nothing is stored against edge protection or within 1 m of the loading point.

  6. Stairs are kept clear; use the handrail; do not carry items that block your view or need both hands.

Stage 5 – Manual handling

  1. Use the forklift, pallet trucks, sack trucks, trolleys, dollies and panel carts wherever possible (H8).

  2. Assess each lift (Task, Individual, Load, Environment). If it is heavy, bulky, long or awkward, get help or a handling aid.

  3. Long profile and staging decks are handled by two people; one person calls each lift.

  4. Wear cut-resistant gloves for profile and sharp edges.

Stage 6 – Profile cleaning area

  1. Cleaning is done only in the designated cleaning area, which is ventilated and away from battery charging and ignition sources.

  2. Use the product named on the COSHH sheet, at the right dilution, decanted only into labelled containers (H21).

  3. Wear chemical gloves and eye protection; respirator only if the COSHH sheet says.

  4. Flammable products stay in the flammables cabinet when not in use; solvent-soaked cloths go in the lidded metal bin.

  5. Profile is cleaned on trestles or benches at waist height, with long lengths lifted on by two people.

Stage 7 – Tools and electrical equipment

  1. Only use tools you have been shown how to use. Check before use: guards fitted, leads and plugs undamaged, PAT label in date.

  2. Use cordless tools where possible. Wear eye protection for drilling and cutting, and a respirator for cutting or sanding wood and MDF (SSOW-03).

  3. Use safety knives with retractable or shielded blades; cut away from the body; never leave open blades lying around.

  4. Defective tools or equipment are tagged "Do not use" and handed to the Warehouse Manager.

  5. No overloaded sockets or daisy-chained extension leads.

Stage 8 – Forklift charging and LPG

  1. Batteries are charged only at the designated charging point, which is ventilated, signed, with no smoking or naked flames, and kept clear of stock and waste.

  2. Battery topping up and LPG cylinder changes are done only by trained staff, wearing the PPE in SSOW-03, never alone (H21, H19).

Stage 9 – Visitors, drivers and contractors

  1. All visitors sign in, are given hi-vis, and are escorted in the warehouse.

  2. Visiting drivers follow SSOW-01: report on arrival, hand over keys, and wait in the driver safe area.

  3. Contractors provide their own RAMS for their work, receive a site induction, and are supervised. Hot work needs a permit (H19).

Stage 10 – End of day

  1. Forklift parked in its bay: forks lowered, handbrake on, key removed and stored securely; put on charge if needed.

  2. Walkways and fire exits left clear; waste removed; spills cleaned.

  3. Tools and equipment switched off and put away; chargers off unless needed overnight (lithium-ion tool batteries are not left on charge overnight).

  4. Flammables cabinet closed; cleaning area tidy.

  5. Building checked for people, doors and shutters closed and locked, alarm set. Any lone worker checks out with their buddy (SSOW-02).

Emergencies

Situation Action
Fire or fire alarm Stop work; forklift parked clear of exits with forks lowered; leave by the nearest exit to the assembly point; do not re-enter (H19)
Injury Call a first aider; call 999 for serious injuries; do not move the person unless in danger; preserve the scene
Racking struck or collapsing Warn others and clear the area; do not try to hold or unload a collapsing bay; isolate the area and report
Chemical splash or spill Eyes: eyewash for at least 15 minutes. Skin: wash with water. Spill: contain with the spill kit, ventilate, follow the SDS (H21)
Intruder or aggressive person Do not confront; move to a safe place; call 999

All accidents, near misses and racking damage are reported to the Warehouse Manager the same day and recorded; RIDDOR-reportable incidents are reported to HSE by the Managing Director.

Inspections and checks

Racking expert inspection Annually SEMA-approved inspector (SARI) Inspection report

Document control

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
SOP reference SOP-04 – Warehouse Operations
Linked SSOW SSOW-04 – Warehouse Operations
Version 1.0
Prepared by James Pickard (Managing Director)
Approved by Mathew Pickard (Director)
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner if SSOW-04 changes, after an accident or near miss, or when the equipment or task changes

1. Purpose

This SOP sets out the standard way we run the warehouse at Unit 1, Brickyard Road every day, from opening up to locking up, so everyone works the same way. The hazards, risk ratings and controls are in SSOW-04 – Warehouse Operations, which must be read with this SOP.

2. Scope

This SOP covers general day-to-day warehouse work. Higher-risk tasks have their own SSOWs, SOPs and risk assessments.

Applies to:

  • Employees, agency and casual crew, visiting drivers, contractors and visitors.
  • The warehouse floor, racking, mezzanine, profile cleaning area, forklift charging point, loading area and yard at Unit 1, Brickyard Road.
  • Receiving, storing, picking and preparing event equipment; returns from events; checking, cleaning and repairing stock; moving loads by hand, trolley, pallet truck and forklift; housekeeping and waste.

Does not cover:

  • Forklift operation, loading and unloading vehicles and visiting driver arrangements in detail (SOP-01 / SSOW-01 – Forklift Loading and Unloading).
  • Lone working arrangements (SOP-02 / SSOW-02 – Lone Working).
  • PPE selection and care in detail (SOP-03 / SSOW-03 – Personal Protective Equipment).
  • Work at height in detail (H5 – Working at Height) and chemical assessments (H21 – COSHH).

3. Responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Approves SSOW-04 and this SOP; provides resources, equipment and training; makes sure inspections are carried out; reports RIDDOR incidents to HSE
Warehouse Manager Runs the warehouse day to day; inducts new staff; carries out the daily and weekly checks; keeps records; stops unsafe work
Forklift operators Follow SSOW-01; keep to forklift routes; travel at walking pace; give way to pedestrians at crossings
All warehouse staff and crew Follow this SOP and SSOW-04; wear PPE (SSOW-03); keep the warehouse tidy; report hazards, damage and near misses
First person in Carries out and records the opening-up checks (or the Warehouse Manager does)
Visitors and contractors Sign in; are escorted; wear the hi-vis and PPE provided; follow instructions

4. Definitions

Term Meaning
Walkway Marked pedestrian route on the warehouse floor
Crossing point Marked place where pedestrians may cross a forklift route
Exclusion zone Marked area where nobody may stand, such as a forklift working area or below the mezzanine loading point
SWL Safe working load shown on the load notice for each racking bay and beam level, or in kg/m² for the mezzanine
SEMA traffic light system Grading of racking damage: red, amber or green
SARI SEMA-approved racking inspector who carries out the annual expert inspection
Pallet safety gate Gate at the mezzanine loading point; one side is always closed
COSHH sheet Assessment sheet stating the product, dilution and PPE for a chemical

5. Competence and authorisation

  • Every new employee, agency or casual worker has a warehouse induction on their first day, before starting work. It covers the warehouse rules, walkways and crossing points, fire exits and assembly point, first aid, welfare facilities, PPE and how to report hazards. The induction is recorded.
  • Only authorised, certificated operators use the forklift (SSOW-01).
  • Pallet trucks, power tools and the profile cleaning area are used only after instruction.
  • Only use tools you have been shown how to use.
  • Battery topping up and LPG cylinder changes are done only by trained staff, never alone.
  • Young workers (under 18) and new starters are supervised and do not use the forklift, work at height or work alone.
  • Staff and crew are briefed on SSOW-04 and this SOP, and their signatures are recorded.

6. Equipment, PPE and materials

Item Requirement
Hi-vis and safety footwear At all times on the warehouse floor, mezzanine, loading area and yard
Gloves For handling; cut-resistant for profile and sharp edges
Chemical gloves and eye protection In the profile cleaning area; respirator only if the COSHH sheet says
Eye protection For drilling and cutting
Respirator For cutting or sanding wood and MDF (SSOW-03)
Hard hat In overhead work zones
Handling aids Pallet trucks, sack trucks, trolleys, dollies and panel carts
Steps or podium Approved type, for low racking levels only (H5)
Spill kit Available for cleaning up spills straight away
Cones and “Do not use” tags For coning off unsafe areas and tagging defective equipment
Flammables cabinet and lidded metal bin For flammable products and solvent-soaked cloths

7. Procedure

Follow these steps every day. The warehouse rules displayed at the entrance apply throughout.

7.1 Opening up and daily checks

  1. Check the building. The first person in (or the Warehouse Manager) checks the building is secure with no signs of break-in, leaks or damage overnight.
  2. Check lights and fire safety. Confirm lights work throughout the warehouse, mezzanine and yard; fire exits are unlocked and clear; the fire alarm panel shows no faults; extinguishers are in place.
  3. Check the floor and racking. Confirm walkways, aisles and crossing points are clear with markings visible, there are no spills, loose packaging or trip hazards, and no obvious racking damage or overloaded bays.
  4. Check the mezzanine and first aid. Confirm mezzanine edge protection and the pallet gate are intact and working, and the first aid kit and eyewash are available.
  5. Confirm the forklift pre-use check. The forklift operator completes the pre-use check before use (SSOW-01).
  6. Record and report. Record the checks on the daily warehouse checklist. Report any defect to the Warehouse Manager, and cone off or tag out of use anything that makes an area unsafe until fixed.

Hold point: Do not use any area or equipment found unsafe in the opening-up checks until it has been fixed. New starters do not start work until their induction is complete and recorded.

7.2 Moving around the warehouse

  1. Wear hi-vis and safety footwear. Office staff entering the warehouse put on hi-vis and check for forklift movement first; keep doors between the warehouse and office closed.
  2. Use the walkways. Walk in marked walkways and cross forklift routes only at marked crossing points.
  3. Stop, look, make eye contact. Before crossing, look both ways and make eye contact with any forklift driver. Wait until the driver has stopped or signalled you on.
  4. Keep out of forklift areas. Never enter a forklift working area or exclusion zone, or walk under raised forks or loads.
  5. No phones or headphones. Do not use mobile phones or wear headphones while walking on forklift routes or operating equipment.
  6. Drive at walking pace. Forklift operators travel at walking pace, sound the horn at blind corners, doorways and the ends of aisles, and give way to pedestrians at crossings.

7.3 Housekeeping and returns

  1. Keep routes clear. Keep walkways, aisles, crossing points, fire exits, extinguishers, call points, electrical panels and first aid points clear. Nothing is stored in walkways, even temporarily.
  2. Clean as you go. Put packaging, shrink wrap, straps and offcuts in the correct bin as soon as you finish with them.
  3. Deal with spills at once. Clean up spills straight away with the spill kit, or cone them off and report them.
  4. Route cables safely. Route trailing cables away from walkways or cover them with cable protectors.
  5. Process returns. Unload event returns to the designated returns area, then check and put them away by the end of the next working day.
  6. Remove waste. Take waste to the external skips at least daily. Do not let cardboard and plastic build up inside the building.

7.4 Storage and racking

  1. Check the load notice. Load each bay and beam level within the SWL on its load notice. If there is no load notice, do not use the bay.
  2. Place pallets squarely. Place pallets squarely on beams with no overhang beyond the manufacturer’s limit. Do not use damaged pallets.
  3. Heavy low, light high. Put heavy items on lower levels and light items higher. Store nothing on top of racking unless it is designed for it.
  4. Secure loose items. Box, shrink-wrap or restrain loose items on upper levels so they cannot fall.
  5. Store long items horizontally. Store profile, truss and poles on cantilever or profile racking, never leaning against walls or racking.
  6. Keep stacks stable. Keep free-standing stacks of cases or boxes stable and no higher than about 1.8 m (or 3 times the base width, whichever is less) unless designed to stack higher.
  7. Never climb racking. Use the forklift (SSOW-01), or approved steps or a podium for low levels (H5).
  8. Report racking damage. Report any impact, bent upright or beam, missing beam lock or loose floor fixing straight away. Unload and tape off the bay until checked. Damage is graded red (unload at once and isolate), amber (unload as soon as possible, repair within 4 weeks) or green (monitor).

Hold point: Do not use a bay with no load notice, or a damaged or taped-off bay, until it has been checked and cleared by the Warehouse Manager.

7.5 Mezzanine

  1. Keep within the SWL. Keep stored items within the SWL (kg/m²) displayed at the stairs and loading point, spread evenly. Store nothing against edge protection or within 1 m of the loading point.
  2. Move goods by forklift. Move goods to and from the mezzanine by forklift through the pallet safety gate, not up or down the stairs.
  3. Operate the gate correctly. Close the operator side whenever the loading side is open. Never tie or wedge the gate open.
  4. Keep clear of the edge and below. Do not lean over the gate or edge protection, or stand in the marked exclusion zone below the loading point during loading.
  5. Use the stairs safely. Keep the stairs clear, use the handrail and do not carry items that block your view or need both hands.

Hold point: Do not open the loading side of the pallet gate unless the operator side is closed.

7.6 Manual handling and cleaning profile

  1. Use handling aids. Use the forklift, pallet trucks, sack trucks, trolleys, dollies and panel carts wherever possible (H8).
  2. Assess each lift. Consider Task, Individual, Load and Environment. If it is heavy, bulky, long or awkward, get help or a handling aid.
  3. Team lift long items. Handle long profile and staging decks with two people; one person calls each lift. Wear cut-resistant gloves.
  4. Clean in the designated area only. Use the ventilated cleaning area, away from battery charging and ignition sources, with profile on trestles or benches at waist height.
  5. Use the right product. Use the product named on the COSHH sheet at the right dilution, decanted only into labelled containers, wearing chemical gloves and eye protection (H21).
  6. Store flammables. Keep flammable products in the flammables cabinet when not in use and put solvent-soaked cloths in the lidded metal bin.

7.7 Tools, electrical equipment and charging

  1. Check tools before use. Confirm guards are fitted, leads and plugs are undamaged and the PAT label is in date. Use cordless tools where possible.
  2. Cut safely. Use safety knives with retractable or shielded blades, cut away from the body and never leave open blades lying around.
  3. Tag defects. Tag defective tools or equipment “Do not use” and hand them to the Warehouse Manager.
  4. Avoid overloading. Do not overload sockets or daisy-chain extension leads.
  5. Charge at the charging point. Charge forklift batteries only at the designated charging point, kept clear of stock and waste, with no smoking or naked flames. Battery topping up and LPG cylinder changes are done only by trained staff in SSOW-03 PPE, never alone.

7.8 Visitors, drivers and contractors

  1. Sign in and escort visitors. All visitors sign in, are given hi-vis and are escorted in the warehouse.
  2. Direct visiting drivers. Visiting drivers report on arrival, hand over keys and wait in the driver safe area (SSOW-01).
  3. Control contractors. Contractors provide their own RAMS, receive a site induction and are supervised. Hot work needs a permit (H19).

7.9 End of day

  1. Park the forklift. Park in its bay with forks lowered, handbrake on, key removed and stored securely; put on charge if needed.
  2. Leave the floor clear. Leave walkways and fire exits clear, waste removed and spills cleaned.
  3. Switch off and put away. Switch off and put away tools and equipment. Turn chargers off unless needed overnight; do not leave lithium-ion tool batteries on charge overnight.
  4. Close down the cleaning area. Close the flammables cabinet and leave the cleaning area tidy.
  5. Lock up. Check the building for people, close and lock doors and shutters, and set the alarm. Any lone worker checks out with their buddy (SSOW-02).

Hold point: Do not set the alarm and leave until the building has been checked for people.

8. Completion checks

Check Standard
Walkways, aisles and fire exits Clear, with nothing stored in them
Spills and waste Spills cleaned; waste in external skips
Returns Checked and put away by end of the next working day
Racking All bays within SWL; any damage reported and bay taped off
Mezzanine Within SWL; pallet gate working and not wedged open
Forklift Parked in bay, forks lowered, handbrake on, key secured
Tools and chargers Switched off and put away; no lithium-ion batteries charging overnight
Flammables Cabinet closed; cleaning area tidy
Building Checked for people, locked and alarmed

9. If something goes wrong

Situation Action
Fire or fire alarm Stop work; park forklift clear of exits with forks lowered; leave by the nearest exit to the assembly point; do not re-enter (H19)
Injury Call a first aider; call 999 for serious injuries; do not move the person unless in danger; preserve the scene
Racking struck or collapsing Warn others and clear the area; do not try to hold or unload a collapsing bay; isolate the area and report
Chemical in the eyes Use the eyewash for at least 15 minutes
Chemical on the skin Wash with water
Chemical spill Contain with the spill kit, ventilate and follow the SDS (H21)
Intruder or aggressive person Do not confront; move to a safe place; call 999
Accident or near miss Report to the Warehouse Manager the same day; it is recorded, and RIDDOR incidents are reported to HSE by the Managing Director

See SSOW-04 – Warehouse Operations for the full emergency arrangements.

10. Records

documents.html:
Document details

This safe system of work sets out how Pickard Event Services forklifts are operated safely: who may drive them, the checks before use, and how to travel, lift, stack, park and charge. Loading and unloading vehicles is covered separately in SSOW-01; this SSOW covers every other forklift task.

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
Reference SSOW-05 – Forklift Operation
Locations Unit 1, Brickyard Road (warehouse, racking, mezzanine loading point, loading area and yard) and event sites where Pickard operates a forklift
Equipment Counterbalance forklift trucks (battery-electric or LPG), with fork extensions or other attachments where fitted
Tasks Moving pallets, stillages, flight cases and equipment; putting away and retrieving from racking; loading and unloading the mezzanine; moving long loads; daily checks, parking and charging or refuelling
Persons at risk Forklift operators, pedestrians and warehouse staff, visiting drivers, contractors and visitors
Assessor James Pickard
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner after an accident or near miss, a new truck or attachment, or a change to the warehouse layout

Key legislation and guidance: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999; Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER); Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations 1998 (LOLER); Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992; HSE L117 (Rider-operated lift trucks – operator training and safe use, Approved Code of Practice); HSE HSG136 (A guide to workplace transport safety); HSE INDG457 (Use lift trucks safely); Fork Lift Truck Association (FLTA) guidance; DSEAR 2002 (LPG).

Roles and responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Approves this SSOW; provides suitable trucks, training, LOLER thorough examinations and servicing
Warehouse Manager Authorises operators in writing; holds the keys; checks daily check sheets; arranges refresher training; takes defective trucks out of use; stops unsafe operation
Forklift operator Holds a valid certificate and written authorisation; carries out the daily check; operates the truck as set out below; reports defects and incidents
Banksman / marshal Guides the operator where vision is restricted; controls pedestrians around the working area
All staff and visitors Keep to walkways; wear hi-vis; keep clear of forklift working areas; never ride on or approach a moving truck

Hazards and risk ratings

Risk = Likelihood (L) × Severity (S), each scored 1–5, as in the H-series risk assessments. Ratings are residual risk, with this SSOW followed. Striking a pedestrian and truck overturn carry the highest residual risk (5, Medium) because the outcome could be fatal.

Score Likelihood Severity
1 Very unlikely Trivial – no treatment needed
2 Unlikely Minor – first aid only
3 Possible Moderate – medical treatment, up to 7 days off work
4 Likely Major – RIDDOR-reportable or over-7-day injury
5 Almost certain Fatal or permanent disability
Risk score Rating Action required
1–4 Low Maintain current controls; review annually
5–9 Medium Controls adequate but monitor; improve where reasonably practicable
10–16 High Further controls needed before or alongside work; management attention
20–25 Very high Stop work until risk is reduced
Ref Hazard Main controls (stage of this SSOW) Residual L × S Rating
FL1 Truck striking a pedestrian Walkways and crossings, horn and lights, walking-pace speed, banksman, hi-vis (Stage 2) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
FL2 Truck overturning (lateral or longitudinal) Rated capacity, loads low and tilted back, no turning on slopes, seatbelt (Stages 2, 3, 5) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
FL3 Load falling from the forks Correct fork spacing, load secured, mast tilted back, smooth handling (Stage 3) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
FL4 Collision with racking, the mezzanine or structures Slow speed, clear sight, column guards, banksman (Stages 2, 4) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
FL5 Falls from the mezzanine during loading Pallet safety gate, exclusion zone below, H5 (Stage 4) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
FL6 Truck failure (brakes, hydraulics, chains) Daily pre-use check, servicing, LOLER examination (Before work starts) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
FL7 Fire or explosion during battery charging or LPG change Ventilated charging point, no ignition sources, trained staff only (Stage 7) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
FL8 Operator crushed or injured when leaving or mounting the truck Three points of contact; never jump down; truck fully stopped (Stage 6) 1 × 3 = 3 Low
FL9 Long loads striking people or objects Spreader or fork extensions, banksman, extra clearance (Stage 3) 1 × 4 = 4 Low

Before work starts

Competence and authorisation

  • Only operators who hold a current certificate from an accredited training body (RTITB, AITT, ITSSAR or NPORS) for counterbalance trucks, and written authorisation from the Warehouse Manager, may operate a forklift.

  • Before authorisation, each operator has familiarisation on the specific truck and any attachments, and a site induction covering the warehouse layout, routes, racking, mezzanine and charging point.

  • Refresher training or reassessment every 3–5 years, and sooner after an accident, near miss, poor practice, a long break from driving, or a new type of truck.

  • Operators must be fit to drive: not unwell, overtired, or affected by alcohol, drugs or medication. Anyone with a medical condition that could affect safe driving tells the Managing Director in confidence.

  • Nobody under 18 operates a forklift except as part of supervised accredited training.

  • Forklift keys are kept in a secure place and issued only to authorised operators.

Personal protective equipment

Hi-vis and safety footwear at all times (SSOW-03). Gloves for handling loads and straps. Hard hat in overhead work zones or where the venue requires it. The truck's seatbelt is worn at all times while driving.

Daily pre-use check (operator, start of each shift)

The operator checks the truck before use and records the result on the daily check sheet. Any defect = truck not used. The key is removed, the truck is tagged "Do not use", and the Warehouse Manager is told.

Area Check
Walk-round No damage, leaks (oil, hydraulic fluid, battery acid) or loose parts; overhead guard intact
Tyres and wheels No cuts, chunks missing or excessive wear; wheel nuts secure; pneumatic tyres at correct pressure
Forks and carriage Forks not cracked, bent or worn at the heel; fork locking pins in place; carriage and backrest undamaged
Mast and chains Chains evenly tensioned, lubricated, no damaged links; mast rollers and channels undamaged
Hydraulics Lift, lower and tilt work smoothly; no leaks from hoses, rams or fittings
Brakes Service brake and parking brake hold the truck
Steering Smooth with no excessive play
Safety devices Horn, lights, flashing beacon, reversing alarm working; seatbelt and seat switch working
Battery (electric) Charge level adequate; cables, plugs and connectors undamaged; battery restraint in place
LPG (gas trucks) Cylinder secure in its cradle; hose and connector undamaged; no smell of gas
Data plates Rated capacity plate (and attachment plates) present and legible
Attachments Fork extensions or spreaders correctly fitted and secured; marked with their own capacity

Safe system of work – step by step

Stage 1 – Mounting and starting

  1. Check the area around the truck is clear of people and obstructions.

  2. Mount using the step and handholds, keeping three points of contact. Never use the steering wheel or controls as a handhold.

  3. Adjust the seat and mirrors, and fasten the seatbelt.

  4. Check all controls are in neutral, the forks are lowered and the parking brake is on, then start the truck.

  5. Test the brakes and steering at low speed before starting work.

Stage 2 – Travelling

  1. Travel with the forks lowered to about 150 mm from the ground and the mast tilted back, loaded or unloaded.

  2. Keep to forklift routes. Drive at walking pace inside the warehouse, and adjust speed for the floor, the load, visibility and people nearby.

  3. Look in the direction of travel at all times. If the load blocks your forward view, travel in reverse, or use a banksman.

  4. Sound the horn at blind corners, doorways, the ends of racking aisles and where pedestrians may be.

  5. Give way to pedestrians at crossing points. If a person enters your path, stop and wait.

  6. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles (at least three truck lengths), and do not overtake at junctions, blind spots or in aisles.

  7. Keep all parts of your body inside the truck's overhead guard.

  8. Slow down before turning; never turn sharply at speed or with a raised load.

  9. Watch for overhead hazards: doorways, the mezzanine, sprinklers, lights and cables.

  10. Do not use a mobile phone or headphones while operating.

Stage 3 – Picking up, carrying and setting down loads

  1. Check the load weight and its load centre against the rated capacity plate. If the weight is unknown or close to the limit, do not lift it; ask the Warehouse Manager. Remember that attachments, lift height and load centre reduce capacity.

  2. Check the load is stable, secured (strapped or shrink-wrapped if needed) and on a sound pallet.

  3. Approach the load squarely and slowly, with forks level and at the right height.

  4. Set the fork spacing to suit the load, as wide as possible for stability.

  5. Insert the forks fully under the load (at least two-thirds of the load length, and fully for heavy loads), with the load against the backrest.

  6. Lift the load just clear, tilt the mast back, check behind, then reverse out slowly.

  7. Lower to travel height before moving off. Never travel or turn with a load raised.

  8. To set down, stop squarely at the location, level the forks, lower the load gently, and withdraw the forks straight back.

  9. Long loads (aluminium profile, truss, staging): use fork extensions or a spreader bar rated for the load, centre the load, travel slowly, use a banksman to watch both ends, and allow extra clearance when turning.

  10. Never push or drag loads with the forks, or use the forks to open doors or move other vehicles.

Stage 4 – Racking and the mezzanine

  1. Stop square to the racking bay, with the parking brake on, before raising a load. Only raise or lower a load with the truck stationary.

  2. Raise the load to just above the beam level, move forward slowly until the load is over the beams, level the forks, lower the load onto the beams, and withdraw.

  3. Do not exceed the beam or bay load shown on the racking load notice. Do not place loads where they overhang the beam beyond the manufacturer's limit.

  4. Report any impact with racking straight away, however small. The bay is unloaded and taped off until checked (SSOW-04).

  5. Mezzanine loading: use only the pallet safety gate. Before raising a load, check the operator side of the gate is closed and nobody is standing near the loading point above or below. Place the load fully inside the gate, lower it, withdraw, and lower the forks before moving away. Nobody stands under the raised load (H5, SSOW-04).

  6. Use a banksman whenever the view of the forks, load or racking is restricted.

Stage 5 – Slopes, ramps and outdoor ground

  1. Travel straight up and down slopes and ramps. Never turn on a slope or travel across it.

  2. On a slope with a load: travel with the load facing uphill (forwards up, reverse down). Without a load: forks facing downhill.

  3. Outdoors: check the ground is firm and level, and watch for potholes, drains, kerbs, soft ground and ice. Do not operate in high wind with high or light, bulky loads.

Stage 6 – Parking and leaving the truck

  1. Park only in the designated parking bay or a safe place: on level ground, not blocking walkways, fire exits, fire equipment or racking aisles.

  2. Lower the forks fully to the ground with the tips tilted forward, apply the parking brake, put controls in neutral, switch off and remove the key.

  3. Dismount facing the truck with three points of contact. Never jump down.

  4. If leaving the truck for even a short time, lower the forks and remove the key.

  5. At the end of the day, return the key to its secure place.

Stage 7 – Battery charging and LPG changes

  1. Battery charging: only at the designated charging point (ventilated, no smoking or naked flames, clear of stock). Park, switch off, remove the key, open the battery cover if the manufacturer says, connect the charger, and switch on. Never disconnect a battery while the charger is on.

  2. Battery topping up: only by trained staff, with distilled or deionised water and a filling gun, after charging. Wear acid-resistant gloves and a face shield or goggles; eyewash available (H21).

  3. LPG cylinder change: only by trained staff, outdoors or in a well-ventilated area, away from drains and ignition sources, with the engine off. Close the cylinder valve, change the cylinder, check the connector and seal, open the valve and check for leaks. Wear gloves to protect against cold burns. Store cylinders upright in the outdoor cage (H19, H21).

  4. None of these tasks is done alone (SSOW-02).

Banksman hand signals

Signal Meaning
Both arms raised, palms forward Stop
Arms beckoning towards the body Come towards me
Arms pushing away from the body Move away from me
One arm pointing left or right, other beckoning Move in that direction
Hand raised, palm up, moving upward Raise forks
Hand lowered, palm down, moving downward Lower forks
Hands held apart, closing together Distance closing – slow down
Arms crossed in front of the chest Emergency stop

If the operator loses sight of the banksman, stop immediately.

Never

  • Never operate a forklift without a valid certificate, written authorisation and a completed daily check.

  • Never carry passengers, or lift anyone on the forks, a pallet or a cage not designed and approved for the truck.

  • Never exceed the rated capacity, or add counterweight to lift more.

  • Never travel or turn with the load raised, or turn on a slope.

  • Never let anyone stand or walk under raised forks or a raised load.

  • Never raise or lower a load while the truck is moving.

  • Never drive with an obstructed forward view; reverse or use a banksman.

  • Never leave the truck with the forks raised, the engine running or the key in.

  • Never use a defective truck, or alter or disable any safety device (seatbelt, seat switch, alarms).

  • Never use a mobile phone or headphones while operating.

  • Never operate the forklift while working alone (SSOW-02).

Emergencies

Situation Action
Truck starts to tip over Stay in the seat with the seatbelt on. Hold the steering wheel firmly, brace your feet, and lean away from the direction of the fall. Never jump out
Load falls or starts to fall Stay in the cab; do not try to catch it; warn others; stop work and report
Pedestrian struck or injured Stop at once; switch off; call a first aider and 999 for serious injuries; do not move the truck or the person unless in danger; preserve the scene
Racking struck Stop; lower the load if safe; warn others; isolate the bay; report (SSOW-04)
Truck fault while working Stop in a safe place, lower the forks, switch off, remove the key, tag "Do not use", report
Battery fire or LPG leak Switch off and close the cylinder valve if safe; evacuate; raise the fire alarm; call 999 (H19)
Fire alarm Lower the forks, park clear of exits and walkways, switch off, remove the key, evacuate

All accidents, near misses, racking impacts and truck damage are reported to the Warehouse Manager the same day and recorded; RIDDOR-reportable incidents are reported to HSE by the Managing Director.

Maintenance, examination and records

Item Frequency By whom Record kept
Daily pre-use check Each shift Operator Daily check sheet (kept 12 months)
Routine service As manufacturer (typically every 3–6 months or by hours run) Competent forklift engineer Service record
LOLER thorough examination At least every 12 months (every 6 months if used to lift people or with lifting attachments) Competent person Thorough examination report (kept until the next one, and at least 2 years)
Battery and charger inspection As manufacturer Competent person Service record
Operator certificates and authorisations On issue; refresher every 3–5 years Warehouse Manager Operator authorisation register

  • H5 – Working at Height (mezzanine loading)

  • H19 – Fire (charging and LPG)

  • H21 – COSHH (battery acid, LPG)

Action plan

Keys Set up secure key storage with issue only to authorised operators Warehouse Manager Ongoing
FL6 Confirm LOLER examination and service dates; diarise the next ones Managing Director Ongoing
FL6 Introduce the daily check sheet and keep completed sheets for 12 months Warehouse Manager Ongoing
FL1 Mark forklift routes, crossing points and the parking bay; fit a blue spot or warning light if pedestrian traffic is heavy Warehouse Manager June 26
FL9 Confirm fork extensions or spreaders are rated, marked and added to the capacity plate Warehouse Manager Ongoing

documents.html:
Document control

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
SOP reference SOP-05 – Forklift Operation
Linked SSOW SSOW-05 – Forklift Operation
Version 1.0
Prepared by James Pickard (Managing Director)
Approved by Mathew Pickard (Director)
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner if SSOW-05 changes, after an accident or near miss, or when the equipment or task changes

1. Purpose

This SOP gives the standard method for operating Pickard Event Services forklifts, so every operator checks, drives, lifts, stacks, parks and charges the truck the same way, every time. The hazards, risk ratings and controls are in SSOW-05 – Forklift Operation, which must be read with this SOP.

2. Scope

This SOP covers all forklift work other than loading and unloading vehicles.

Applies to:

  • Forklift operators, banksmen and anyone working near forklifts.
  • The warehouse, racking, mezzanine, loading area and yard, and event sites.
  • Counterbalance forklift trucks (battery-electric or LPG), with fork extensions or other attachments where fitted.
  • Moving loads, racking and mezzanine work, long loads, daily checks, parking, charging and refuelling.

Does not cover:

  • Loading and unloading vehicles with a forklift – see SOP-01 / SSOW-01 – Forklift Loading and Unloading.
  • General warehouse work and racking inspection – see SOP-04 / SSOW-04 – Warehouse Operations.

3. Responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Provides suitable trucks, training, LOLER thorough examinations and servicing; reports RIDDOR incidents to HSE
Warehouse Manager Authorises operators in writing; holds and issues keys; checks daily check sheets; arranges refresher training; takes defective trucks out of use; stops unsafe operation
Forklift operator Holds a valid certificate and written authorisation; carries out the daily check; follows this SOP; reports defects and incidents
Banksman / marshal Guides the operator where vision is restricted; controls pedestrians around the working area
All staff and visitors Keep to walkways; wear hi-vis; keep clear of forklift working areas; never ride on or approach a moving truck

4. Definitions

Term Meaning
Rated capacity plate The plate on the truck (and each attachment) showing its maximum load
Load centre Where the load’s weight sits on the forks; it affects capacity
Travel height Forks lowered to about 150 mm from the ground with the mast tilted back
Banksman The person who guides the operator by hand signals and controls pedestrians
Three points of contact Two hands and one foot, or two feet and one hand, on the truck when mounting or dismounting
Pallet safety gate The gate at the mezzanine loading point; the only place loads are lifted to the mezzanine
Daily check sheet The record of the operator’s pre-use check, completed each shift

5. Competence and authorisation

  • Only operators who hold a current certificate from an accredited training body (RTITB, AITT, ITSSAR or NPORS) for counterbalance trucks, and written authorisation from the Warehouse Manager, may operate a forklift.
  • Before authorisation, each operator has familiarisation on the specific truck and any attachments, and a site induction covering the warehouse layout, routes, racking, mezzanine and charging point.
  • Refresher training or reassessment is every 3–5 years, and sooner after an accident, near miss, poor practice, a long break from driving, or a new type of truck.
  • Operators must be fit to drive: not unwell, overtired, or affected by alcohol, drugs or medication. Anyone with a medical condition that could affect safe driving tells the Managing Director in confidence.
  • Nobody under 18 operates a forklift except as part of supervised accredited training.
  • Battery topping up and LPG cylinder changes are done only by trained staff.
  • Forklift keys are kept in a secure place and issued only to authorised operators.

6. Equipment, PPE and materials

Item Requirement
Forklift truck Counterbalance truck, serviced and LOLER-examined; daily check passed
Attachments Rated for the load, fitted, secured and capacity-marked
Hi-vis and safety footwear Worn at all times (SSOW-03)
Gloves For handling loads and straps
Hard hat In overhead work zones or where the venue requires it
Seatbelt Worn at all times while driving
Battery topping-up kit Distilled or deionised water, filling gun, acid-resistant gloves, face protection, eyewash
LPG cylinders Changed with gloves on (cold burns); stored upright in the outdoor cage
Daily check sheet and “Do not use” tag Available at the start of each shift

7. Procedure

Carry out the following steps in order. Never operate a forklift while working alone (SSOW-02).

7.1 Before the shift

  1. Confirm you are fit and authorised. Only start if you hold a current certificate and written authorisation, and you are fit to drive.
  2. Collect the key and put on PPE. Obtain the key from its secure place, and wear hi-vis and safety footwear, with gloves and a hard hat where required.
  3. Carry out and record the daily pre-use check. Check the walk-round, tyres and wheels, forks and carriage, mast and chains, hydraulics, brakes, steering, safety devices, battery or LPG, data plates and attachments, as listed in SSOW-05, and complete the daily check sheet for the shift.

Hold point: If any defect is found, do not use the truck. Remove the key, tag the truck “Do not use” and tell the Warehouse Manager.

7.2 Mounting and starting

  1. Check the area. Make sure the area around the truck is clear of people and obstructions.
  2. Mount safely. Use the step and handholds with three points of contact; never use the steering wheel or controls as a handhold.
  3. Set up and start. Adjust the seat and mirrors and fasten the seatbelt. Check all controls are in neutral, the forks are lowered and the parking brake is on, then start.
  4. Test brakes and steering. Test both at low speed before starting work.

7.3 Travelling

  1. Travel at travel height. Keep the forks about 150 mm from the ground with the mast tilted back, loaded or unloaded.
  2. Keep to routes and speed. Use forklift routes and drive at walking pace inside the warehouse, adjusting for the floor, load, visibility and people nearby.
  3. Keep a clear view. Look in the direction of travel at all times; if the load blocks your forward view, travel in reverse or use a banksman.
  4. Warn and give way. Sound the horn at blind corners, doorways, racking aisle ends and where pedestrians may be; give way at crossing points and stop if anyone enters your path.
  5. Keep your distance. Stay at least three truck lengths from other vehicles and do not overtake at junctions, blind spots or in aisles.
  6. Turn and travel with care. Slow down before turning, never turn sharply at speed or with a raised load, keep your body inside the overhead guard, and watch for doorways, the mezzanine, sprinklers, lights and cables. Do not use a mobile phone or headphones while operating.

7.4 Picking up, carrying and setting down loads

  1. Check the weight. Check the load weight and load centre against the rated capacity plate, allowing for attachments and lift height. If the weight is unknown or close to the limit, do not lift; ask the Warehouse Manager.
  2. Check the load. Make sure it is stable, secured (strapped or shrink-wrapped if needed) and on a sound pallet.
  3. Approach and set the forks. Approach squarely and slowly with the forks level at the right height, spaced as wide as possible for the load.
  4. Pick up and lower to travel height. Insert the forks fully under the load (at least two-thirds of its length, fully for heavy loads) with the load against the backrest; lift just clear, tilt back, check behind and reverse out slowly. Lower to travel height before moving off; never travel or turn with a load raised.
  5. Set down. Stop squarely, level the forks, lower the load gently and withdraw the forks straight back.
  6. Handle long loads correctly. For aluminium profile, truss or staging, use rated fork extensions or a spreader bar, centre the load, travel slowly, use a banksman to watch both ends and allow extra clearance when turning.
  7. Use the forks only for lifting. Never push or drag loads, open doors or move other vehicles with the forks.

Hold point: Do not lift any load until its weight and load centre are confirmed within the rated capacity of the truck and any attachment.

7.5 Racking and the mezzanine

  1. Stop, then place the load. Stop square to the bay with the parking brake on; only raise or lower a load with the truck stationary. Raise to just above beam level, move forward slowly until over the beams, level the forks, lower onto the beams and withdraw.
  2. Respect racking limits. Do not exceed the beam or bay load on the racking load notice, or overhang the beam beyond the manufacturer’s limit.
  3. Report racking impacts. Report any impact straight away, however small; the bay is unloaded and taped off until checked (SSOW-04).
  4. Load the mezzanine through the gate only. Place the load fully inside the pallet safety gate, lower it, withdraw, and lower the forks before moving away.
  5. Use a banksman when vision is restricted. Follow the agreed hand signals in SSOW-05; if you lose sight of the banksman, stop immediately.

Hold point: Before raising a load to the mezzanine, check the operator side of the pallet safety gate is closed and nobody is near the loading point above or below. Nobody stands under the raised load (H5, SSOW-04).

7.6 Slopes, ramps and outdoor ground

  1. Travel straight on slopes. Travel straight up and down; never turn on a slope or travel across it.
  2. Face the right way. With a load, keep the load facing uphill (forwards up, reverse down); without a load, forks facing downhill.
  3. Check outdoor ground. Check the ground is firm and level and watch for potholes, drains, kerbs, soft ground and ice; do not operate in high wind with high or light, bulky loads.

7.7 Parking and leaving the truck

  1. Park in a safe place. Use the designated parking bay or level ground clear of walkways, fire exits, fire equipment and racking aisles.
  2. Make the truck safe. Lower the forks fully with the tips tilted forward, apply the parking brake, put controls in neutral, switch off and remove the key. Do this even if leaving the truck for a short time.
  3. Dismount safely. Face the truck with three points of contact; never jump down.
  4. Return the key. At the end of the day, return the key to its secure place.

7.8 Battery charging and LPG changes

  1. Charge at the charging point only. Use the designated, ventilated charging point, clear of stock, with no smoking or naked flames. Park, switch off, remove the key, open the battery cover if the manufacturer says, connect the charger and switch on. Never disconnect a battery while the charger is on.
  2. Top up after charging (trained staff only). Use distilled or deionised water and a filling gun, wearing acid-resistant gloves and a face shield or goggles, with eyewash available (H21).
  3. Change LPG cylinders safely (trained staff only). Work outdoors or in a well-ventilated area away from drains and ignition sources, engine off. Close the valve, change the cylinder, check the connector and seal, open the valve and check for leaks, wearing gloves. Store cylinders upright in the outdoor cage (H19, H21).

Hold point: Do not charge, top up or change an LPG cylinder alone (SSOW-02).

8. Completion checks

Check Standard
Daily check sheet Completed for the shift; any defect reported and truck tagged “Do not use”
Loads placed Square, stable and within racking limits
Mezzanine Loads fully inside the pallet safety gate; forks lowered before moving away
Racking Any impact reported; affected bay unloaded and taped off
Truck parked Safe place, forks down, brake on, switched off
Key Removed from the truck and returned to its secure place at the end of the day
Charging or LPG Charger connected; no LPG leaks; cylinders in the outdoor cage
Incidents Reported to the Warehouse Manager the same day

9. If something goes wrong

Situation Action
Truck starts to tip over Stay in the seat with the seatbelt on; hold the wheel, brace your feet, lean away from the fall; never jump out
Load falls or starts to fall Stay in the cab; do not try to catch it; warn others; stop work and report
Pedestrian struck or injured Stop; switch off; call a first aider and 999 for serious injuries; do not move the truck or person unless in danger; preserve the scene
Racking struck Stop; lower the load if safe; warn others; isolate the bay; report (SSOW-04)
Truck fault while working Stop in a safe place, lower the forks, switch off, remove the key, tag “Do not use”, report
Battery fire or LPG leak Switch off and close the cylinder valve if safe; evacuate; raise the fire alarm; call 999 (H19)
Fire alarm Lower the forks, park clear of exits and walkways, switch off, remove the key, evacuate
Lost sight of banksman Stop immediately

Report all accidents, near misses, racking impacts and truck damage to the Warehouse Manager the same day so they are recorded; the Managing Director reports RIDDOR-reportable incidents to HSE. See SSOW-05 for the full emergency arrangements.

10. Records

Record Completed by Kept by
Daily check sheet (each shift) Operator Warehouse Manager (kept 12 months)
Service record (routine service, as manufacturer) Competent forklift engineer Managing Director
Thorough examination report (LOLER, at least every 12 months, or 6 months if used to lift people or with lifting attachments) Competent person Managing Director (until the next one, and at least 2 years)
Battery and charger inspection (as manufacturer) Competent person Managing Director (service record)
Operator authorisation register (on issue; refresher every 3–5 years) Warehouse Manager Warehouse Manager
Accident, near miss and damage reports Operator / Warehouse Manager Warehouse Manager
