documents.html:
Document details

This safe system of work sets out how Pickard Event Services builds and breaks down shell scheme stands: the aluminium modular system of uprights, rails and infill panels used to create exhibition stands, booths and partition walls. Shell scheme is light and quick to build, but walls are unstable until they are braced by corners and rails, the rails and fascias are fitted at height, and the work is done in busy halls alongside forklifts and other contractors. The main dangers are falls from access equipment, walls or panels toppling, manual handling of long components, and being struck by vehicles during build-up and breakdown.

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
Reference SSOW-11 – Shell Scheme Build (Aluminium Modular Construction)
Equipment Aluminium uprights (posts), horizontal rails and extrusions, infill wall panels, fascia boards and name boards, bracing rails, doors, store rooms, shelving and counter units, locking tools and hand tools, podium steps, hop-ups and step ladders
Locations Event sites (exhibition halls, conference venues, marquees) and Unit 1, Brickyard Road (preparing, picking, cleaning and storing kit)
Tasks Planning and picking kit; marking out; erecting uprights and wall panels; fitting rails, bracing rails and fascias at height; fitting shelves, doors and name boards; inspection and handover; breakdown, packing and return
Persons at risk Build crew, supervisors, other contractors, venue staff, exhibitors and, during open periods, visitors
Assessor James Pickard
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner after an accident or near miss, a change in the system or access equipment used, or a change in venue rules

Key legislation and guidance: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999; Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (CDM, which applies to event build and breakdown); Work at Height Regulations 2005; Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992; Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER); Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992 (as amended 2022); Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; the system manufacturer’s assembly instructions and load data; the venue’s rules and the organiser’s event manual; The Event Safety Guide (the Purple Guide); the e-Guide (event industry guidance for exhibitions).

Roles and responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Approves this SSOW; provides trained crew, suitable access equipment and resources; makes sure CDM duties are agreed with the organiser for each event
Build supervisor (named for each event) Plans the build from the floor plan; briefs the crew; controls the build area and the order of work; checks stability and quality; signs off each stand before handover; liaises with the organiser, venue and other contractors
Warehouse Manager Picks and checks kit against the floor plan; quarantines damaged components; keeps access equipment inspected; organises loading (SSOW-01, SSOW-04)
Build crew Have been trained in shell scheme assembly and the access equipment they use; follow this SSOW and the build supervisor’s instructions; carry out pre-use checks; report damage, defects and incidents
Electrician / Responsible Person (SSOW-10) Fits and tests stand lighting and sockets on the shell scheme, in coordination with the build supervisor
Organiser / venue Provides the floor plan, build schedule and site rules; acts as principal contractor or appoints one under CDM; controls vehicle movements in the hall

Hazards and risk ratings

Risk = Likelihood (L) × Severity (S), each scored 1–5, as in the H-series risk assessments. Ratings are residual risk, with this SSOW followed. Falls while fitting rails and fascias at height carry the highest residual risk (8, Medium), followed by walls toppling during build and breakdown (6, Medium); handling long components and trips over kit are the most common minor injuries.

Score Likelihood Severity
1 Very unlikely Trivial – no treatment needed
2 Unlikely Minor – first aid only
3 Possible Moderate – medical treatment, up to 7 days off work
4 Likely Major – RIDDOR-reportable or over-7-day injury
5 Almost certain Fatal or permanent disability
Risk score Rating Action required
1–4 Low Maintain current controls; review annually
5–9 Medium Controls adequate but monitor; improve where reasonably practicable
10–16 High Further controls needed before or alongside work; management attention
20–25 Very high Stop work until risk is reduced
Ref Hazard Main controls (stage of this SSOW) Residual L × S Rating
SH1 Falls from access equipment when fitting rails, bracing rails and fascias Podium steps or hop-ups with guardrails as first choice; step ladders for short, light tasks only; never stand on the structure, panels or furniture (H5; Stage 4) 2 × 4 = 8 Medium
SH2 Walls or panels toppling during build or breakdown Build from a corner so every wall line has a return; fit rails as each section goes up; no unbraced free-standing runs; breakdown in reverse order (Stages 3, 4, 7) 2 × 3 = 6 Medium
SH3 Rails, fascias, tools or fixings falling from height Two people for long components at height; area below kept clear; tools kept in pouches, not left on top of rails (Stage 4) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
SH4 Manual handling of long or awkward components and panel stacks Two-person carries for rails and fascias; trolleys and pallet trucks for stacks; panels moved in manageable numbers (H8; Stages 2, 7, 8) 2 × 2 = 4 Low
SH5 Struck by forklifts and vehicles in the hall during build-up and breakdown Hi-vis; follow venue traffic routes; work within the stand area; stay clear of forklift operations (SSOW-01, SSOW-05; Stages 2, 7) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
SH6 Cuts, pinches and trapped fingers from extrusions, panel edges and locks Gloves; correct locking tool; damaged components quarantined; fingers clear when sliding panels into channels (Stages 3, 4) 2 × 2 = 4 Low
SH7 Slips and trips over kit, packaging, carpet edges and cables Kit staged in one area; packaging and waste removed as work goes; carpet edges taped; cables routed under SSOW-10 (all stages) 2 × 2 = 4 Low
SH8 Structure overloaded by shelves, graphics, lights or exhibitors’ items Manufacturer’s load data followed; shelves within rated load; exhibitors told what can be fixed to the walls; nobody climbs or leans ladders on the structure (Stages 5, 6) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
SH9 Electric shock from stand lighting and sockets Fitted and tested only by electricians under SSOW-10; crew do not wire or alter electrics (Stage 5) 1 × 5 = 5 Medium
SH10 Fire spread from stand materials or blocked exits Flame-retardant panels and materials as required by the venue; gangways, exits and extinguishers kept clear; lights clear of fascias and graphics (H19; Stages 1, 5) 1 × 4 = 4 Low
SH11 Fatigue from long, early or overnight build and breakdown shifts Planned shifts and breaks; work rotated; supervisor stops anyone too tired to work safely (all stages) 2 × 2 = 4 Low
SH12 Cleaning solutions used on aluminium profile at the warehouse COSHH assessment followed; gloves and eye protection; good ventilation (H21; Stage 8) 1 × 2 = 2 Low

Before work starts

Training and competence

  • Only crew trained in shell scheme assembly (this SSOW, the system’s components and locking method, stability rules and the order of build) may build or break down shell scheme. New starters work alongside an experienced builder until the build supervisor signs them off.
  • Podium steps, hop-ups and step ladders are used only by crew briefed on them (H5).
  • A build supervisor is named for every event and is on site throughout build-up and breakdown.

Planning (build supervisor, before the event)

  1. Get the floor plan, stand list, build schedule, venue rules and event manual from the organiser. Confirm who is principal contractor under CDM and what paperwork (risk assessments, method statements, crew lists) the organiser needs.
  2. Check the floor plan for wall heights, stand sizes, open sides, doors, store rooms, fascias and any bracing rails, and that gangway widths and fire exits are not affected.
  3. Plan the order of build: which stands go up first, where kit will be staged, and how the build fits around forklift deliveries, carpet laying, electrics and other trades.
  4. Plan access equipment for every high-level task (podium steps or hop-ups with guardrails as standard).
  5. Plan crew numbers, shifts and breaks so nobody works excessive hours (SH11).
  6. Confirm that panels and materials meet the venue’s fire safety requirements (for example flame-retardant certificates).

Kit preparation (warehouse, before dispatch)

Any damaged or incomplete item = not sent. Quarantine it, tag it “Do not use” and report it to the Warehouse Manager.

Item Check
Uprights and rails Straight, no dents, cracks or splits in the extrusion; locks turn and grip; ends undamaged
Panels Not warped, cracked or delaminated; edges intact; correct size and colour
Fascias and name boards Undamaged; correct lengths for the stands
Shelving, doors and counters Brackets, hinges and locks complete and working
Tools Correct locking tools for the system; hand tools in good condition
Access equipment Podiums, hop-ups and steps: feet, treads, locks and guardrails sound
Quantity Kit counted against the pick list for the floor plan, plus a small spare

Kit is loaded and secured for transport as in SSOW-01, SSOW-07 and SSOW-08.

Personal protective equipment

  • Safety footwear with toe caps and hi-vis, as required in all halls during build-up and breakdown (SSOW-03).
  • Gloves with good grip for handling extrusions and panels.
  • Hard hats where there is overhead work by others or when working below people fitting at height, or where the venue requires them.

Safe system of work – step by step

Stage 1 – Arrival and marking out

  1. Sign in, attend the venue induction, and confirm fire exits, assembly points, first aid, welfare facilities and the hall’s vehicle routes.
  2. The build supervisor briefs the crew on the floor plan, the order of build, access equipment, the stand areas and any hazards from other trades.
  3. Mark out stand positions from the floor plan and the hall’s grid marks. Check that gangway widths, fire exits, fire points and hydrants are kept clear before anything goes up.

Stage 2 – Unloading and staging kit

  1. Unload in the area and at the time set by the venue, using forklifts, pallet trucks or tail lifts as in SSOW-01, SSOW-05, SSOW-06 and SSOW-09. Keep clear of forklift operations.
  2. Stage kit in one tidy area per block of stands, out of gangways and fire routes. Stand panels on edge in racks or lay them flat; never lean stacks against walls where they can slide.
  3. Carry rails and fascias with two people, one at each end, looking where you are going. Move panel stacks and heavy items on trolleys or pallet trucks (H8).

Stage 3 – Uprights and wall panels

  1. Start each wall line from a corner, so that every section has a return and is self-supporting as it goes up.
  2. Stand the first upright, slide the panel into its channel, add the next upright and lock it. Keep fingers clear of the channels when sliding panels in.
  3. Lock every connection fully with the correct tool. Check each upright is vertical and fully seated on the floor.
  4. Never leave a straight run of wall standing without a return, a temporary prop or a rail. If work stops part way, brace the section or take it down.
  5. Keep the area around a wall under construction clear of other people.

Stage 4 – Rails, bracing rails and fascias (work at height)

  1. Fit the top rails as soon as each section of wall is up, to lock the structure together.
  2. Use podium steps or hop-ups with guardrails as the first choice. Use step ladders only for short, light tasks, set up on level ground at the correct angle, facing the work, and never on top of other equipment (H5).
  3. Never stand on, climb or lean ladders against the shell scheme, panels, counters or furniture.
  4. Fit fascias, long rails and bracing rails with two people, one at each end, each on their own access equipment. Keep the area below clear of others.
  5. Keep tools in a pouch; never leave tools or fixings on top of rails.

Stage 5 – Fit-out

  1. Fit shelves, doors, store rooms, counters and name boards to the manufacturer’s instructions. Do not exceed the rated load on shelves or brackets.
  2. Stand lighting and sockets are fitted, connected and tested only by electricians under SSOW-10. Crew do not wire, alter or move electrical items.
  3. Tape carpet edges, remove packaging and waste as you go, and keep gangways clear.
  4. Keep lights clear of fascias, name boards and graphics as set out by the electrician.

Stage 6 – Inspection and handover

  1. The build supervisor walks every stand and checks: uprights locked and vertical, rails fitted, panels secure, no loose or missing parts, shelves and doors secure, and gangways and fire exits clear.
  2. Put right any faults before handover. Record the check on the stand sign-off sheet.
  3. Tell exhibitors what they may fix to the walls (for example light graphics with approved hooks or Velcro), and that they must not climb on, cut, drill or overload the structure.
  4. During the open period, any changes are made only by Pickard Event Services crew, outside open hours or with the area cordoned off.

Stage 7 – Breakdown

  1. Start only when the organiser allows it and the stand has been cleared of exhibitors’ goods. Electricians isolate and remove stand electrics first (SSOW-10).
  2. Work in reverse order of build: name boards, shelves and fit-out items first, then fascias and rails (two people, from access equipment), then panels and uprights.
  3. Take walls down section by section from the open end towards the corner, keeping each remaining section braced by a return or rail. Never pull or push walls over.
  4. Stack, count and pack kit as it comes down, and tag damaged parts “Do not use”.
  5. Keep clear of forklifts and vehicles entering the hall during breakdown; load out as in Stage 2.

Stage 8 – Return, cleaning and storage

  1. Unload at Unit 1, Brickyard Road, check kit against the pick list, and report missing or damaged items to the Warehouse Manager.
  2. Clean aluminium profile and panels using the products and controls in the COSHH assessment (H21).
  3. Store kit in its racks or stillages, with heavy items low down and nothing overhanging walkways (SSOW-04).

Never

  • Never build or break down shell scheme without training and a briefing from the build supervisor.
  • Never leave a wall standing without a return, a rail or a prop.
  • Never stand on, climb or lean ladders against the shell scheme, panels, counters or furniture.
  • Never use a step ladder for long or heavy tasks at height, or stand on its top steps.
  • Never fit long rails or fascias at height on your own.
  • Never leave tools or fixings on top of rails.
  • Never pull or push walls over at breakdown.
  • Never block gangways, fire exits, fire points or extinguishers with kit or stands.
  • Never wire, alter or move stand electrics; that is for the electrician (SSOW-10).
  • Never use damaged components or overload shelves and fittings.
  • Never work in the path of forklifts or vehicles in the hall.

Emergencies

Situation Action
Fall from height Do not move the casualty if a back, neck or head injury is possible; call the venue first aiders and 999 for a serious injury; make the area safe
Wall or panel starting to topple Shout a warning; step clear; do not try to catch a falling wall; once it is down, check for injuries before clearing it
Person struck or trapped Make the area safe and stop nearby vehicles; free them only if it is safe; first aid and 999 as needed
Cut or crush injury First aid from the venue or the crew first aider; report and record it
Fire alarm Stop work, leave kit, evacuate by the nearest exit to the assembly point; do not return until told it is safe (H19)

All accidents, near misses and damage are reported to the build supervisor and recorded the same day, and to the venue as their rules require. RIDDOR-reportable incidents are reported to HSE by the Managing Director.

documents.html:
Document control

Item Detail
Company JNM Events Ltd t/a Pickard Event Services
SOP reference SOP-11 – Shell Scheme Build (Aluminium Modular Construction)
Linked SSOW SSOW-11 – Shell Scheme Build (Aluminium Modular Construction)
Version 1.0
Prepared by James Pickard (Managing Director)
Approved by Mathew Pickard (Director)
Date issued Jan 2026
Next review Jan 2027, or sooner if SSOW-11 changes, after an accident or near miss, or when the equipment or task changes

1. Purpose

This SOP sets out the standard method Pickard Event Services uses to plan, build, hand over, break down and return aluminium shell scheme stands, booths and partition walls. It makes sure every crew builds in the same order and to the same stability rules. Hazards, risk ratings and controls are set out in SSOW-11 – Shell Scheme Build (Aluminium Modular Construction), which must be read with this SOP.

2. Scope

This SOP covers the whole shell scheme job, from planning and picking kit to build-up, handover, breakdown and return.

Applies to:

  • Build supervisors, build crew and the Warehouse Manager.
  • Event sites (exhibition halls, conference venues, marquees) and Unit 1, Brickyard Road.
  • Shell scheme components, fit-out items, locking and hand tools, podium steps, hop-ups and step ladders.

Does not cover:

  • Fitting, connecting, testing or removing stand lighting and sockets – see SOP-10 / SSOW-10 – Temporary Electrical Installations.
  • Forklift, pallet truck and tail lift use – see SOP-01, SOP-05, SOP-06 and SOP-09.
  • Securing kit for transport – see SOP-01, SOP-07 and SOP-08.

3. Responsibilities

Role Responsibilities
Managing Director (James Pickard) Approves this SOP; provides trained crew, suitable access equipment and resources; agrees CDM duties with the organiser for each event; names a build supervisor for every event; reports RIDDOR incidents to HSE
Build supervisor (named for each event) Plans the build from the floor plan; briefs the crew; controls the build area and order of work; checks stability and quality; signs off each stand before handover; liaises with the organiser, venue and other contractors
Warehouse Manager Picks and checks kit against the floor plan; quarantines damaged components; keeps access equipment inspected; organises loading
Build crew Follow this SOP and the build supervisor’s instructions; carry out pre-use checks; report damage, defects and incidents
Electrician / Responsible Person Fits, tests, isolates and removes stand lighting and sockets under SSOW-10, in coordination with the build supervisor
Organiser / venue Provides the floor plan, build schedule and site rules; acts as or appoints the principal contractor under CDM; controls vehicle movements in the hall

4. Definitions

Term Meaning
Shell scheme The aluminium modular system of uprights, rails and infill panels used to build exhibition stands, booths and partition walls
Upright A vertical aluminium post that holds the wall panels in its channels
Rail A horizontal aluminium member that locks the uprights and panels together
Bracing rail A cross member fitted to brace the structure, as shown on the floor plan
Fascia The board fitted along the top front of a stand, often carrying the name board
Return A wall at an angle to a wall line, such as a corner, that makes the section self-supporting
Build supervisor The person named for each event who controls the build and signs off each stand
Stand sign-off sheet The record of the build supervisor’s inspection of each stand before handover

5. Competence and authorisation

  • Only crew trained in shell scheme assembly may build or break down shell scheme. Training covers SSOW-11, the system’s components and locking method, the stability rules and the order of build.
  • New starters work alongside an experienced builder until the build supervisor signs them off.
  • Podium steps, hop-ups and step ladders are used only by crew briefed on them (H5).
  • A build supervisor is named for every event and is on site throughout build-up and breakdown.
  • Crew training is given on induction, with a refresher every 3 years, and recorded by the Managing Director.

6. Equipment, PPE and materials

Item Requirement
Shell scheme kit Checked and picked as in section 7.2; damaged items quarantined
Panels and materials Meet the venue’s fire safety requirements
Tools Correct locking tools; hand tools in good condition; tool pouch
Access equipment Podium steps or hop-ups with guardrails first; step ladders for short, light tasks only
Handling aids Trolleys and pallet trucks for panel stacks and heavy items
Safety footwear and hi-vis Worn in all halls during build-up and breakdown (SSOW-03)
Gloves Good-grip gloves for handling extrusions and panels
Hard hat When others work overhead, below people fitting at height, or where the venue requires it
Cleaning products Only those in the COSHH assessment (H21), with gloves and eye protection

7. Procedure

Follow these stages in order, and the referenced SOPs for linked tasks.

7.1 Planning (build supervisor, before the event)

  1. Get the event information. Obtain the floor plan, stand list, build schedule, venue rules and event manual from the organiser. Confirm who is principal contractor under CDM and what paperwork the organiser needs.
  2. Check the floor plan. Check wall heights, stand sizes, open sides, doors, store rooms, fascias and bracing rails, and confirm gangway widths and fire exits are not affected.
  3. Plan the order of build. Decide which stands go up first, where kit will be staged, and how the build fits around forklift deliveries, carpet laying, electrics and other trades.
  4. Plan access, crew and shifts. Allocate podium steps or hop-ups with guardrails for every high-level task. Plan crew numbers, shifts and breaks so nobody works excessive hours. Make sure panels and materials meet the venue’s fire safety requirements, with flame-retardant certificates available.

7.2 Kit preparation (warehouse, before dispatch)

  1. Pick and check the kit. Count kit against the pick list for the floor plan, plus a small spare. Check uprights and rails are straight with no dents, cracks or splits and locks that turn and grip; panels are not warped, cracked or delaminated; fascias and name boards are undamaged and the right length; fittings, tools and access equipment are complete and sound.
  2. Quarantine defects. Do not send any damaged or incomplete item. Tag it “Do not use” and report it to the Warehouse Manager.
  3. Load for transport. Load and secure kit as in SOP-01, SOP-07 and SOP-08.

7.3 Arrival and marking out

  1. Sign in and attend the induction. Sign in at the venue, attend the venue induction, and confirm fire exits, assembly points, first aid, welfare facilities and the hall’s vehicle routes.
  2. Attend the crew briefing. The build supervisor briefs the crew on the floor plan, order of build, access equipment, stand areas and any hazards from other trades, and records it on the briefing sheet.
  3. Mark out the stands. Mark out stand positions from the floor plan and the hall’s grid marks. Check that gangway widths, fire exits, fire points and hydrants are clear before anything goes up.

Hold point: Do not start any build work until the crew has been briefed by the build supervisor and the briefing sheet completed.

7.4 Unloading and staging kit

  1. Unload as directed. Unload in the area and at the time set by the venue, using forklifts, pallet trucks or tail lifts as in SOP-01, SOP-05, SOP-06 and SOP-09. Wear hi-vis, follow venue traffic routes and keep clear of forklift operations.
  2. Stage kit tidily. Stage kit in one area per block of stands, out of gangways and fire routes. Stand panels on edge in racks or lay them flat; never lean stacks against walls where they can slide.
  3. Carry long items with two people. Carry rails and fascias with one person at each end, looking where you are going. Move panel stacks and heavy items on trolleys or pallet trucks.

7.5 Uprights and wall panels

  1. Start from a corner. Start each wall line from a corner, so every section has a return and is self-supporting as it goes up.
  2. Build the wall. Stand the first upright, slide the panel into its channel, add the next upright and lock it. Keep fingers clear of the channels when sliding panels in.
  3. Lock and check every connection. Lock every connection fully with the correct tool. Check each upright is vertical and fully seated on the floor.
  4. Never leave a run unbraced. Never leave a straight run of wall standing without a return, a temporary prop or a rail. If work stops part way, brace the section or take it down. Keep other people away from a wall under construction.

Hold point: No wall line may go up except from a corner, and no section may be left standing without a return, a rail or a prop.

7.6 Rails, bracing rails and fascias (work at height)

  1. Fit top rails straight away. Fit the top rails as soon as each section of wall is up, to lock the structure together.
  2. Choose the right access equipment. Use podium steps or hop-ups with guardrails as the first choice. Check them before each use and tag any defect “Do not use”.
  3. Use step ladders correctly. Use step ladders only for short, light tasks, set up on level ground at the correct angle, facing the work, never on top of other equipment and never standing on the top steps.
  4. Stay off the structure. Never stand on, climb or lean ladders against the shell scheme, panels, counters or furniture.
  5. Fit long items with two people. Fit fascias, long rails and bracing rails with two people, one at each end, each on their own access equipment. Keep the area below clear of others.
  6. Control tools. Keep tools in a pouch; never leave tools or fixings on top of rails.

Hold point: Do not lift a fascia, long rail or bracing rail into position until a second person is in place at the other end on their own access equipment and the area below is clear.

7.7 Fit-out

  1. Fit stand furniture. Fit shelves, doors, store rooms, counters and name boards to the manufacturer’s instructions. Do not exceed the rated load on shelves or brackets.
  2. Leave electrics to the electrician. Stand lighting and sockets are fitted, connected and tested only by electricians under SOP-10 / SSOW-10. Do not wire, alter or move electrical items.
  3. Keep the area tidy. Tape carpet edges, remove packaging and waste as you go, and keep gangways clear. Cables are routed by the electrician. Keep lights clear of fascias, name boards and graphics as set out by the electrician.

7.8 Inspection and handover

  1. Inspect every stand. The build supervisor walks every stand and checks the items in section 8, puts right any faults before handover, and records the check on the stand sign-off sheet.
  2. Brief the exhibitor. Tell exhibitors what they may fix to the walls (for example light graphics with approved hooks or Velcro), and that they must not climb on, cut, drill or overload the structure.
  3. Control changes during the open period. Only Pickard Event Services crew make changes, outside open hours or with the area cordoned off.

Hold point: No stand is handed over until the build supervisor has inspected it and completed the stand sign-off sheet.

7.9 Breakdown

  1. Wait for clearance. Start only when the organiser allows it, the stand has been cleared of exhibitors’ goods and electricians have isolated and removed stand electrics (SOP-10 / SSOW-10). The build supervisor briefs the crew and records it on the briefing sheet.
  2. Work in reverse order. Remove name boards, shelves and fit-out items first, then fascias and rails (two people, from access equipment), then panels and uprights.
  3. Take walls down section by section. Work from the open end towards the corner, keeping each remaining section braced by a return or rail. Never pull or push walls over.
  4. Pack and load out. Stack, count and pack kit as it comes down, and tag damaged parts “Do not use”. Keep clear of forklifts and vehicles entering the hall, and load out as in section 7.4.

Hold point: Breakdown does not start until the organiser allows it, exhibitors’ goods are cleared and stand electrics have been removed; it then follows reverse order of build only.

7.10 Return, cleaning and storage

  1. Check kit in. Unload at Unit 1, Brickyard Road, check kit against the pick list, and report missing or damaged items to the Warehouse Manager.
  2. Clean the kit. Clean aluminium profile and panels using the products and controls in the COSHH assessment (H21), with gloves, eye protection and good ventilation.
  3. Store the kit. Store kit in its racks or stillages, with heavy items low down and nothing overhanging walkways (SOP-04).

8. Completion checks

Check Standard
Uprights Locked, vertical and fully seated on the floor
Rails and bracing rails All fitted and locked; no loose or missing parts
Panels Secure in their channels; no damage
Shelves, doors and counters Secure and within rated load
Gangways and fire exits Clear, with fire points and extinguishers unobstructed
Housekeeping Carpet edges taped; packaging and waste removed
Sign-off Stand sign-off sheet completed by the build supervisor
Kit returned Counted against pick list; damage logged and quarantined; stored correctly

9. If something goes wrong

Situation Action
Fall from height Do not move the casualty if a back, neck or head injury is possible; call venue first aiders and 999 for a serious injury; make the area safe
Wall or panel starting to topple Shout a warning and step clear; do not try to catch it; once down, check for injuries before clearing it
Person struck or trapped Make the area safe and stop nearby vehicles; free them only if safe; first aid and 999 as needed
Cut or crush injury First aid from the venue or crew first aider; report and record it
Fire alarm Stop work, leave kit, evacuate by the nearest exit to the assembly point; do not return until told it is safe
Damaged component found Stop using it, tag it “Do not use” and report it to the build supervisor or Warehouse Manager
Crew member too tired to work safely The build supervisor stops them working

Report all accidents, near misses and damage to the build supervisor, record them the same day, and report them to the venue as their rules require. The Managing Director reports RIDDOR-reportable incidents to HSE. See SSOW-11 for the full emergency arrangements.

10. Records
